title: Automated triage + tiered approval flow for low-risk MSA/DPA redlines; linked pricing concession experiment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers and Sales are experiencing long cycle times when small, low-risk MSA/DPA redlines are routed through full legal review. This creates friction for contract velocity and increases time-to-revenue. Objective: Build an automated triage engine + tiered approval flow that (1) classifies redlines into risk buckets, (2) auto-approves low-risk items or routes them to a lightweight commercial approver, and (3) surfaces higher-risk items to Legal. Tie the automated flow to a parallel pricing concession experiment to measure revenue/velocity trade-offs when certain redlines are allowed under pre-approved concession bands.
acceptance_criteria: Rule matrix implemented that maps common MSA/DPA clause edits to risk levels (low/medium/high) with <=5% false-positive rate on a 200-sample validation set
Low-risk edits can be auto-approved by the system and produce a stamped agreement in <24 hours without manual Legal review
Tiered approval path created: auto-approve -> commercial approver -> Legal reviewer, with audit trail and time-to-decision logging
Integration with Security Questionnaire (SQ) and KMS flags: if edit touches security-sensitive clauses, route to Security review automatically
Pricing concession experiment linked: sales UI shows standardized concession bands for auto-approved/low-risk edits and tracks conversion and ARR impact
Legal dashboard shows daily counts, error/appeal rate, and blocked items; SLO for mis-classified high-risk items <1/week after launch
tasks: Draft PRD and rules taxonomy (owner: PM)
Work with Legal to define canonical clause categories and acceptable language variants
Create validation dataset (200 historical redlines + labels) for rules engine
Build lightweight rules engine prototype (engineers + infra)
Implement audit logging and versioned stamped-agreement generation
Add UI for commercial approvers in internal Console (approval queue + reason codes)
Wire pricing concession experiment UI in Sales contract modal and track metrics
Security review integration: gate on SQ flags and KMS/PII clauses
QA: run 3-day shadow run against new deals before enabling auto-approve
Legal sign-off and runbook for appeals/override process
Update KB and Sales enablement materials
rollout_plan: 1) Week 0-2: finalize rules matrix and PRD; 2) Week 3-4: build prototype and validation dataset; 3) Week 5: shadow run against historical/active deals (no auto-approve); 4) Week 6: enable auto-approve for pilot segment (SMB & low-risk templates only) with commercial-approver fallback; 5) Week 7-10: run pricing concession experiment A/B (control vs. auto-approve with 2 concession bands); 6) Week 11: evaluate metrics and expand or rollback
metrics: Appeal rate (percent of auto-approved edits that Legal later flags)
ARR impact from accelerated deals (tracked by RevOps)
Reduction in Legal review hours per week
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mis-classifying high-risk clauses leads to legal exposure. Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds, manual override/appeal flow, and daily Legal audit of auto-approved items.
Risk: Sales gaming concession bands. Mitigation: telemetry alerts for abnormal concession usage and RevOps review cadence.
Risk: Security-sensitive clause bypass. Mitigation: SQ integration and automatic Security hold for flagged edits.
Risk: customer distrust of automated edits. Mitigation: transparency in contract UI and option to request full Legal review
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to low-risk clause categories (indemnity caps, data residency minor text changes, standard subprocessor language) and excludes core changes to liability/indemnity ceilings unless Legal explicitly permits.
We will re-use the redline taxonomy from PM-9571 where applicable but extend for DPA-specific boilerplate
Target initial pilot to customers with ARR < $250k and existing template usage to limit business risk
